New Moon.Behavior: Fish activity often increases during the new moon phase due to the darker nights, allowing fish to feel safer and more actively seek food in shallower waters.
New Moon.Tip: Try fishing in shallow spots as fish may be more present and feeding actively; use natural-colored baits.

Waxing Crescent.Behavior: Fish continue to be moderately active with the increasing light, venturing near the shorelines and shallows.
Waxing Crescent.Tip: Use smaller lures near shorelines, and plan early or late fishing when fish are likely feeding.

First Quarter.Behavior: With the half-lit moon, fish may start moving between shallow and deeper areas, adjusting to the increasing light.
First Quarter.Tip: Experiment with different depths using varied lure sizes to locate active fish.

Waxing Gibbous.Behavior: Fish may reduce activity as moonlight increases, staying deeper or in cover during brighter nights.
Waxing Gibbous.Tip: Fish earlier in the evening or just before dawn, focusing on structures or vegetation cover.

Full Moon.Behavior: Fish are highly active, particularly at night, as the bright moonlight increases their visibility and feeding potential.
Full Moon.Tip: Night fishing can be very productive during the full moon. Use bright lures to take advantage of the well-lit conditions.

Waning Gibbous.Behavior: Fish may still be feeding actively but will gradually reduce shallow movement as moonlight begins to decrease.
Waning Gibbous.Tip: Stick to early morning fishing near cover, as fish might still linger near feeding areas.

Last Quarter.Behavior: Fish activity typically lowers, with fish moving deeper or staying in cover to avoid diminishing moonlight.
Last Quarter.Tip: Focus on deeper areas where fish may be regrouping; slower lures may yield better results.

Waning Crescent.Behavior: Fish tend to conserve energy, waiting out this low-light phase and minimizing shallow water movement.
Waning Crescent.Tip: Fish near structures in mid-depths, and consider larger bait to attract less active fish.
